page.running_head: Sect. I. Part. I. Cap. IV.

main_text.l: in utero materno, Job. 10. v. 8. 10. productio pluviarum, Job. 5. v. 10. & 37. v. 5. & 38. v. 25. Jerem. 10. v. 13. toni-truorum & fulgurum. Jerem. 10. v. 13. Similiter Deo quoq; in scripturis tribuuntur hominum actiones circa praemiorum & poenarum distributionē. Item publica calamitates, quae Causas habent naturales, ut sunt, sterilitates, pestes, inundationes &c. Imo & corda dicitur inclinare quo vult, Proverb. 21. v. 1. operari in nobis velle & perficere, Philip. 2. in ipso vivimus, movemur & sumus. Act. 17. Thomas in caput 5. Johan. illa Christi verba explicans: Pater meus usque modo operatur, & ego operor: docet excludi per illa opinionem dicentium quorundam, Deum mediantibus causis secundis res producere, contra illud Jesa. 26. Omnia opera nostra operatus es in nobis, Domine.

(4) Accedit elegans Augustini testimonium lib. 5. de Genesi ad lit. cap. 20. Movet Deus occulta potentia universam creaturam suam, eoque motu illa ver fata, dum Angeli jussa perficiunt, dum circumeunt sidera, dum alternant venti, dum abyssus aquarum lapsibus agitatur, dum vireta pullulant, suaque semina evolvunt, dum animantia gignuntur, dum iniqui justos exercere permittuntur, explicat secula, qua illi, cum primum condita sunt, tanquam implicita indiderat: qua tamen in suos cursus non explicarentur, si ea ille, qui condidit, provido motu administrare cessaret. Ele-gans quoque illa Dei suum [?] sole comparatio, quam ex Platone colligit, & hoc modo explicat Marsilius Ficinus: Commentario in Convivium Platonis, Orat. 2. cap. 2. Sol, inquit, profecto corpora visibilia & oculos vident-tes procreat, oculis ut videant: lucidum infundit spiritum: Corpora, ut videantur, coloribus pingit. Neque tamen proprius oculis radius, propriiue corporibus colores ad visionem perficiendam
[?] The word after "Dei" is hard to read in the scan; it may be "suum" with a long s-like form.

page.notes: Page 273, Sect. I. Part. I. Cap. IV. The text runs on from the previous page (cont="true") and ends with the catchword "endam". The strip of text at the far left is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Italic passages are judged from the scan. The line "Movet Deus occulta potentia..." and the Ficinus passage are italic in the print, but the exact extent of italic is uncertain. "ver fata" is printed with a space and is left as printed. "Ele-gans" keeps its printed hyphen. The "[?]" after "suum" marks an uncertain word in the printed line "Dei suum sole", which I could not read reliably. The reading "sum" was not confirmed.
